### [S032.U3] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.9 MISCELLANEOUS MATERIALS
- C. Deformed bars for concrete reinforcement and rolled mild steel and medium tensile steel conforming to IS 1139 shall be allowed in the Work provided they are approved by the ER.
- D. Grout: Free of gas-producing or gas-releasing agents, oxidizing catalysts, inorganic accelerators and chlorides. If requested by the ER, grout a sample (1.2m) x(1.2m) x (50mm) plate in the field and demonstrate a minimum of 95% bearing after curing 14 days. Cure grout in accordance with manufacturer's instructions.

### [S045.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT
- A. General: Clean reinforcement of loose rust and mill scale, earth, and other materials that reduce or destroy bond with concrete. Where vapor barrier is required, avoid cutting or puncturing vapor barrier during reinforcement placement and concreting operations.
- B. Position, support, and secure reinforcement against displacement by formwork, construction, or concrete placement operations. Locate and support reinforcing with metal chairs, runners, bolsters, spacers, and hangers, as required. Place reinforcement to obtain the required minimum coverages for concrete protection. Arrange, space, and securely tie bar supports together with (1.6mm) wire to hold reinforcement accurately in position during concrete placement operations. Set wire ties so that twisted ends are directed away from exposed concrete surfaces.

### [S045.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT
- C. Place reinforcing bars having assigned positions so that distinguishing marks agree with those given on the shop drawings relating to or calling for the bars. Provide supports of sufficient number and strength to carry reinforcement. Do not place reinforcing bars more than (50mm) beyond the last leg of any continuous bar support. Do not use supports as bases for runways for concrete conveying equipment or similar construction loads.

### [S048.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT > F. Cover to Reinforcement
1. Reinforcement shall have concrete cover and the thickness of such cover shall be as specified in the Drawings or as directed by the ER.
- G. Fixing in position
1. Correctly cut and bent bars shall be accurately placed in position as detailed in the Drawings. Unless otherwise specified by the ER, reinforcement shall be positioned within the tolerance as under:

### [S048.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT > F. Cover to Reinforcement > G. Fixing in position
- a. for effective depth 200 mm or less  10 mm
- b. for effective depth more than 200 mm  15 mm
2. But in no case shall the cover be reduced by more than 5 mm of that specified. There shall be no compromise on cover for foundation work.
3. Reinforcing bars shall be held in position during the placing of concrete by use of PVC or concrete cover blocks ( made of equal / of higher grade strength of well-cured concrete in use) steel chair spacers, steel hangers, supporting wires, etc. and secured by tying with an annealed binding wire of 16 to 18 gauge as approved by the ER.

### [S048.U4] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT > F. Cover to Reinforcement > G. Fixing in position
5. Binding wire used shall conform to IS 280.
- H. Welded joints or mechanical connections
1. Welded joints or mechanical connections in reinforcement may be used but in all cases or important connections, tests shall be made to prove that the joints are of the full strength of the connected bars. Welding of reinforcement shall be done in accordance with IS recommendation.
2. Where reinforcement bars are bent aside at construction joints and afterwards bent

- back into their original position, care shall be taken to ensure that at no time is the radius of the bend allowed to be less than 4 bar diameters in case of plain mild steel or 6 bar diameters for deformed bars. Care shall be taken when bending back bars to ensure that the concrete around them is not damaged / disturbed.
3. Welding rods used shall conform to IS 814: covered electrodes for metal arc welding of structural steel. Work shall be carried out by a certified welder. Samples from Work site shall be taken at regular intervals and tested. Frequency and number of samples shall be as directed by the ER.

### [S054.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > L. Openings
1. All required openings and block-outs (pockets) shall be provided as detailed in the Drawings. All openings and pockets shall be de-shuttered with care and all corners of openings shall be preserved. All openings / block-outs (pockets) shall be in a correct line and level. After concreting, the openings shall be secured against any accident by proper coverings, guardrails and warning notices, as appropriate.
2. The Contractor shall clean and grout block-outs / pockets at a later date with a nonshrinking grout mix or concrete of matching strength. They shall be well-cured and protected to correct line and level till handling over

### [S060.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING
- A. Independent Testing Agency: A testing agency, engaged at the Contractor's expense, will perform the activities listed herein.
- B. Monitor the Contractor's Quality Control Program. The monitoring activities do not relieve the Contractor of sole responsibility for maintaining the Quality Control Program.

### [S060.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING
- C. Monitoring of Concrete Placement: Continuously observe concrete placement operations on a full-time basis, record such observations on a daily basis, and submit reports of the results.
- D. Monitoring of Contractor's Testing: Monitor Contractor's non-destructive strength testing for form removal and termination of curing.

### [S060.U3] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING
- E. Compression Tests: Sample at point of deposit. Cure the cylinders in laboratory.
1. Additional Cylinders: Furnish a supply of 25 standard cylinder molds at the site at all times for making additional cylinders as may be directed by the ER.
2. Quantity of test cubes and testing
- a. The minimum frequency of cube casting for testing shall be as follows. Each sample shall consist of 6 cubes.

### [S060.U9] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING > b. Three cubes shall be tested on the 7 th day and other three cube...
- e. Compression Test Reports: Present at least the following data in tabular form and distribute immediately after recording the test results.
- 1) Identity of job, Contractor, supplier.
- 2) Identity of mix and required strength.
- 3) Pour location of sampled concrete.
- 4) Slump, water content, air content, truck number, time and date sampled, air temperature, concrete temperature, consistency.

### [S060.U10] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING > b. Three cubes shall be tested on the 7 th day and other three cube...
- 5) Curing history.
- 6) Date tested.
- 7) Compressive strength.
- 8) Type of fracture.
- 9) Compliance with specifications (yes or no)
- F. Slump Tests: First truck each day, each sample for cylinders, and as often as necessary thereafter. Provide a slump cone and rod available for use at all times. Verify water content in accordance with AASHTO T318, "Measurement of Water Content of Fresh Concrete Using the Microwave Oven" as required by the ER, but not less than one test per day.
